chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Mansur ibn Yunus, on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hudhrami, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand letters, each letter opens up one thousand letters, and the thousand [letters] is [but] one letter.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'one thousand letters' taught to Ali by the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the concept of *al-Huruf al-Arba‘a* (the Four Letters) or the esoteric dimensions of the Divine Name, illustrating Ali ibn Abi Talib’s unique spiritual authority (*Wilayah*) as the inheritor of the Prophet’s hidden knowledge. The multiplicative nature of the 'thousand letters' reflects the Shia belief in the infinite depth of the Quran’s inner meanings (*batin*), accessible through the Imams. This narrative underscores the continuity of divine revelation (*Wahy*) and prophetic tradition (*Sunnah*) within the Ahl al-Bayt.
